newsitem.title: USA: Two Marines face assault, rape charges in Oregon.
newsitem.headline: Two Marines face assault, rape charges in Oregon.

text.p: Two Marine sergeants were charged Monday for allegedly attacking a couple on a camping trip in the Mt. Hood National Forest in Oregon.
Henry Thompson, 33, and a 23-year-old Portland woman, both civilians, were assaulted and the woman was raped Saturday near the popular Clear Lake campsite, authorities said.
Sgt. Rudolph Jackson, 28, and Sgt. Clinton Bergmann, 24, were arrested for the assault. They were arraigned Monday.

The Wasco County sheriff's office, which was investigating the incident, said Jackson was arraigned in district court on charges of assault, kidnapping, rape and sexual abuse. Bergmann was charged with assault and kidnapping.

Jackson's bail was set at $200,000 and Bergmann's bail was set at $100,000, Wasco undersheriff Bill Lennox said. Both men were being held in the Wasco County jail in The Dalles, about 80 miles east of Portland.
Bergmann, a recruiter, has been a Marine for six years. Jackson, an administrative clerk, has worked for the corps for eight years.

The two were among 30 Marines and 120 recruits who were in the area for River Strike IV, an annual rafting and camping trip, said Capt. Robert Rice, executive officer for the Marine Station in Portland.
The trips are designed to help new recruits get acquainted with one another, Rice said.
